verdict.rationale: Vercel's own docs say the CLI can be driven "through an automated system," and access tokens authenticate both the CLI and the REST API. Project-scoped tokens are explicitly meant to constrain "jobs, tools, and workflows," which together cover headless and CI automation, alongside git-push deploys. Missing for 10: documented CI-provider guides or non-interactive/token flag usage, and independent or hands-on corroboration of CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Vercel platform using a terminal, or through an automated system
Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf.
This keeps jobs, tools, and workflows constrained to the projects they need rather than granting them the entire team or your full account.
Interact programmatically with your Vercel account using the SDK or direct HTTP requests.
